title: Dynamic Pooling and Regional Participation in Deceased-Donor Organ Allocation
abstract: arXiv:2609.18147v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Moving from geographically fragmented to pooled waiting lists in deceased-donor organ transplantation can improve efficiency, but it raises concerns about regional fairness and participation incentives. This paper studies Pareto gains from such transitions in a multi-class queueing model with impatient agents, perishable items, and a tractable homogeneous compatibility friction. Unlike standard approaches that focus on static match quality or ignore regional incentives in dynamic settings, our analysis identifies dynamic risk pooling as the main source of Pareto improvements for regions: pooling reduces organ waste due to stochastic supply-demand fluctuations, temporal mismatches, and random compatibility outcomes. Although this dynamic surplus theoretically permits Pareto improvements, a purely utilitarian policy that treats all patients equally across regions often fails to deliver them when regions are asymmetric. translated_abstract: 在死亡供体器官移植中，从地理上分散的等待名单转向集中化的等待名单可以提高效率，但这也引发了对区域公平性和参与激励的担忧。本文在一个包含不耐烦主体、易腐物品以及易于处理的同质兼容性摩擦的多类排队模型中，研究了这种转变带来的帕累托改进。与以往关注静态匹配质量或在动态环境中忽略区域激励的标准方法不同，我们的分析识别出动态风险共担是区域实现帕累托改进的主要来源：集中化能够减少由随机供需波动、时间错配以及随机兼容性结果所导致的器官浪费。尽管这种动态剩余在理论上允许实现帕累托改进，但当各区域不对称时，一项在区域间平等对待所有患者的纯粹功利主义政策往往无法实现这一目标。在这种情况下，功利主义
tldr: 本文通过多类排队模型发现，从区域分散转向集中化的器官分配中，动态风险共担（通过减少随机供需波动、时间错配和随机兼容性造成的器官浪费）是区域间帕累托改进的主要来源，但当区域不对称时，纯粹功利主义政策往往无法实现这种帕累托改进。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that dynamic risk pooling—reducing organ waste from stochastic supply-demand fluctuations, temporal mismatches, and random compatibility outcomes—is the main source of Pareto improvements from pooling deceased-donor organ waiting lists, yet purely utilitarian policies often fail to deliver these gains when regions are asymmetric.
